purpose: Independent practice of B1.1 (numbers to 1000) and B1.5 (place value).
student_learning_goal: I can read and represent numbers to 1000 with base-ten blocks and describe each digit's place value.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can read and represent numbers to 1000 with base-ten blocks and describe each digit's place value.
header.character_watermark: Penny the Place Value Pal in the top-right corner with a notebook. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Each scene shows a base-ten block build. Write the number and the expanded form.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Six base-ten block scenes in a 2x3 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Six base-ten block scenes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 3-column grid. Each scene ~2.2in × 1.8in. Pre-fills: B1 — 3 hundred-flats + 4 ten-rods + 7 cubes (347); B2 — 7 flats + 6 tens + 2 cubes (762); B3 — 4 flats + 8 tens + 9 cubes (489); B4 — 9 flats + 0 tens + 5 cubes (905); B5 — 5 flats + 2 tens + 8 cubes (528); B6 — 1 thousand-cube alone (1000).
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; six builds in 2x3 grid.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_SIX_BUILDS: keywords (build, blocks) name what the scenes show.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Place Value of Each Digit
parts.student_instructions: For each number, write what each digit is worth.
parts.visual_layout: Middle. Six numbers stacked, each with place-value lines (Th-H-T-O).

image_placeholders.description: Six number entries in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 0.7in. Format: number on the left in a circle, then four labeled lines (___ Th ___ H ___ T ___ O = ___). Numbers: 405, 909, 200, 1000, 305, 707.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; six entries stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_SIX_NUMBERS: keywords (place-value, digits) name what the entries ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Where do you see 3-digit numbers in your life? Draw and write 2-3 examples.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box for drawing and writing real-life examples.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular drawing box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in, with light-grey solid outline. Penny thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_REAL_LIFE_BOX: keywords (real-life, numbers) name what the box is for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any plausible: '167 days of school', '500 pages in my chapter book', 'street numbers like 142 Oak Street', '750 km from Toronto to Ottawa'.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over. Pick a number between 100 and 1000 and write its expanded form three different ways.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who write B6 as '10' or '100' (missing the thousand-cube) — flag for thousands-place reteach; (b) Part 2 children who skip the zero placeholder (writing '405 = 4 H + 5 O' without showing the 0 in the tens) — flag for the zero-as-structural reteach; (c) Part 3 children who can only think of small numbers — coaching opportunity for everyday numbers.
